The words

Pastor, thou art from us taken
In the glory of thy years,
As the oak, by tempests shaken,
Falls ere time its verdure sears.

Pale and cold we see thee lying
In God's temple, once so dear,
And the mourner's bitter sighing
Falls unheeded on thine ear.

All thy love and zeal, to lead us
Where immortal fountains flow,
And on living bread to feed us,
In our fond remembrance glow.

May the conquering faith, that cheered thee
When thy foot on Jordan pressed,
Guide our spirits while we leave thee
In the tomb that Jesus blessed.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum F and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on d (F), on the first syllable of “Pastor”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 6/4 means six crotchet beats (two dotted minims) in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l and the chromatic fe. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

Lydia Sigourney wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 598 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.

  • Words: Lydia Sigourney (1791–1865)
  • Melody (1631): Gesangbuch, Corner

Tune OMNI DIE (Gesangbuch, Corner); words by Lydia Sigourney (1791–1865).

Questions about Pastor, Thou Art from Us Taken

What is the doh of Pastor, Thou Art from Us Taken?

In this version, in F major, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Pastor, Thou Art from Us Taken start on?

It starts on d (F in F major), a pickup on the first syllable of “Pastor” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is Pastor, Thou Art from Us Taken in the public domain?

Yes. Lydia Sigourney died in 1865; the words were in print by 1853 and the music in 1631. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
